vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: todayhistory
Version: 1.0.1

The skill is a straightforward implementation for querying the Jisu Data 'Today in History' API. The Python script (todayhistory.py) correctly retrieves the API key from environment variables and performs a standard GET request to a legitimate endpoint (api.jisuapi.com) without any signs of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection in the documentation (SKILL.md).

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it queries the Jisu 'Today in History' API, only needs a JISU_API_KEY and python3, and the included script matches the SKILL.md instructions.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the behavior: the code calls https://api.jisuapi.com/todayhistory/query and requires only an API key and python3, which are appropriate for this function.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the included script with a month/day JSON and to set JISU_API_KEY; the script only reads that env var and performs the expected HTTP request. It does not access other files, secrets, or unexpected endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with a bundled Python script and no install spec. The script imports the third-party 'requests' library but the skill does not declare installing this dependency—this is a usability/packaging omission (not a direct security red flag). No downloads or remote installers are used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: it calls the Jisu TodayHistory API and returns results. Before installing, ensure you trust the Jisu API provider because your JISU_API_KEY will be sent to api.jisuapi.com; limit the key's permissions if possible and be ready to revoke it if needed. Note the bundled Python script depends on the 'requests' library but the skill provides no install step—make sure your environment has requests or install it (pip install requests). If you have strict network/privacy requirements, be aware the skill makes outbound HTTP requests to the Jisu API. Otherwise this skill is coherent and proportionate to its stated purpose.
